mainEntity.name: What is compositional balance in photography?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Compositional balance concerns how visual weight is distributed across

a photograph. Size, tone, colour, detail, position, space and subject

meaning influence where attention falls. The resulting stability or

tension should support what the photograph expresses.

mainEntity.name: Does a photograph always need to look balanced?

acceptedAnswer.text:
No. Deliberate dominance or imbalance may express tension, movement or

uncertainty. Compare arrangements and choose according to their effect.

Equal visual weight is not required in every successful photograph.

mainEntity.name: Can a centred subject make a good composition?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Yes. Central placement can support symmetry, directness or stillness.

Compare it with an off-centre arrangement and consider the surrounding

space. Choose the placement that better supports your intention.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between symmetry and balance?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Symmetry concerns mirrored or repeated forms. Balance concerns the

distribution of visual weight. An asymmetrical photograph can feel

balanced, while an apparently symmetrical scene may contain one element

that attracts much more attention.

mainEntity.name: Is the golden ratio better than the rule of thirds?

acceptedAnswer.text:
No overlay guarantees a better photograph. The golden ratio and rule

of thirds suggest arrangements you can compare. Switch the guide off

and judge the resulting relationships, space and meaning within the

image.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to fill empty space to balance a photograph?

acceptedAnswer.text:
No. Space can contribute scale, stillness, isolation or tension without

another object. Compare omission, viewpoint and spacing before adding

a counterweight. Keep an additional element only when it contributes

to the photograph.

mainEntity.name: What gives an element visual weight?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Size, brightness, colour, contrast, detail, sharpness, isolation and

recognisable meaning can all attract attention. Their effects depend

on the surrounding image. A small dark figure against a pale background

may carry considerable weight.

mainEntity.name: How can I practise compositional balance?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Make two versions of one scene: one relatively settled and one allowing

more dominance or tension. Compare the response each supports and

identify a visible reason for your preference. Use that observation

to guide your next photograph.
